name: Beast Academy
line: Beast Academy teaches by lesson and chapter, in a set order. In AMP, teaching and review happen at every problem.
description: AMP vs Beast Academy: Beast Academy teaches by lesson and chapter. In AMP, assessment, teaching and review are continuous, at every problem.
verdict: Beast Academy teaches by lesson and chapter: comic Guide pages and videos teach, a lesson's problems earn stars that open the next lesson, and a chapter test closes each chapter [2][4]. In AMP, assessment, teaching and review are continuous. Every answer updates the learner's level and sets the next problem, and each problem carries its own hint, lesson and worked answer.

reasons.title: Continuous assessment
reasons.body: AMP has no separate test. It places a learner from their first answers, and every answer after updates the learner's level in that part of math and sets the next problem. Beast Academy places a learner with an adaptive test that sets a starting level and chapter [5]. After that, by default, lessons open in a fixed order as stars are earned, and a chapter test closes each chapter [4][7].

reasons.title: The problem is the unit
reasons.body: In AMP, everything a learner needs hangs off the problem in front of them: a hint that gives the first step, a lesson with a worked example, a video lesson, the worked answer afterward, and links to the skills it builds on and leads to. In Beast Academy the unit is the lesson, inside a chapter. Comic Guide pages and videos teach, and a set of problems earns up to three stars [2][4].

reasons.title: A hint before the solution
reasons.body: Each AMP problem carries a hint that gives the first step and never the answer. An answer given after a hint is marked as helped and does not count as learned. In Beast Academy Online, a learner can try again after a wrong answer, and full solutions follow [2][4]. We found no hint system in the pages we read [2][4]. In WestEd's student survey, students asked for more attempts before seeing the answer [10].

reasons.title: Moving on, and going back
reasons.body: In AMP a skill counts as learned when the learner gets it right without help, more than once. Repeated misses send practice back to what the skill builds on. In Beast Academy, one star marks a lesson proficient and opens the next, and the best attempt counts [4][6]. A failed chapter test locks for at least a day before a retry [4]. We found no automatic step back to earlier skills in the pages we read [2][4].

reasons.title: Continuous review
reasons.body: In AMP, learned skills come back in ordinary practice, at growing intervals, mixed with other math. Beast Academy teaches a topic in a chapter and tests it at the chapter's end [4]. Its puzzles give review inside lessons and in a Puzzle Lab [2]. We found no schedule that brings earlier chapters back in the pages we read [3][4]. In a randomized trial with 787 seventh graders, mixed and spaced practice scored 62% a month later, against 38% for practice in blocks [15].

reasons.title: A level for each part of math
reasons.body: AMP keeps a separate level for each part of math and runs from counting through precalculus in one program. A learner further along in geometry than in fractions gets work at both levels. Beast Academy's placement sets a level and a chapter [5]. Its five levels run from ages 6 to 13, and the next step is Prealgebra, a separate AoPS course [1][8].

rows.range: Levels 1 to 5, ages 6 to 13 [1]. Then Prealgebra, a separate AoPS course [8].
rows.start: An adaptive placement test that sets the starting level and chapter [5].
rows.teaching: By lesson: comic-style Guide pages, videos and puzzles, then problems with full solutions [2][9].
rows.next: Lessons open in a fixed order as stars are earned [4]. Parents can switch to open modes [7].
rows.mastery: Up to three stars a lesson, best attempt counting. One star opens the next lesson. A chapter test closes each chapter [4][6].
rows.review: Puzzles inside lessons and in a Puzzle Lab [2]. No scheduled return of earlier chapters found in the pages we read [3][4].
rows.print: A full printed curriculum: Guide and Practice books for each level, with solutions. The same books for every learner [9].
rows.adult: Online, the default order needs no parent, the company says, and it recommends supervision for open modes [7]. With books, the adult assigns the work, by time, not pages [3].
rows.reports: Stars, trophies, problems correct, minutes, and each problem with the learner's response and the solution [6].
rows.evidence: Two studies by outside evaluators, done for its maker: a matched comparison, many users in gifted and high-ability programs, and a usage study without non-users [10][11].

theirs: Beast Academy is a math curriculum for ages 6 to 13 from Art of Problem Solving, in five levels [1]. It comes as printed books, as Beast Academy Online, or both. Its maker calls it a full curriculum, loosely based on the Common Core, built for reasoning and deep understanding rather than drills and memorization [3].

Each level pairs Guide books, which teach in a comic style, with Practice books of exercises, problems and puzzles, with step-by-step solutions [9]. Online, a placement test sets the starting level and chapter [5]. Lessons then open in order by default: each awards up to three stars, one star opens the next lesson, and a chapter test closes each chapter [4][6].
credit: Rich problems and puzzles, with solutions that often show more than one approach [2][9].
A complete printed curriculum a learner can work through away from a screen [9].
It has been studied by evaluators outside the company [10][11].

theirs: WestEd evaluated Beast Academy in 2022, funded by Art of Problem Solving [10]. It compared 547 Mankato Area Public Schools students who used it in both of two school years with non-users matched on a prior MAP score and demographics. Users scored 8.78 points higher on the spring 2021 MAP Growth math test (228.28 against 219.50). Users included students in the district's gifted program and in a program for high-ability students from historically marginalized groups, plus 250 other users. The data are from the COVID years, no effect size in standard deviations is reported, and the authors urge caution in generalizing beyond this group [10]. Art of Problem Solving describes the result as 1 to 2 additional grade levels at 30 minutes a week [12]; the brief reports RIT points and lessons attempted, and we found no grade-level conversion or minutes-per-week figure in it [10].

The Utah Education Policy Center prepared a second study for Art of Problem Solving in 2025 [11]. It analyzed 962 students who used Beast Academy Online in 12 elementary schools of one Utah district, with no group of non-users. After controls, each extra minute of use a month was linked to 0.004 standard deviations on end-of-year tests. The authors call the effects modest and the findings associations, and the report describes them as Promising evidence under ESSA Tier 3 [11].
We found no randomized trial. Beast Academy has no entry in Evidence for ESSA or in What Works Clearinghouse intervention reports [13][14].
ours: In a randomized trial with 787 seventh graders, mixed and spaced practice scored 62% on a test a month later, against 38% for practice in blocks. The What Works Clearinghouse rates the study as meeting its standards without reservations; the test was the researchers' own [15]. AMP applies this at every problem.

AMP's own outcome studies are planned: growth on a national test against hours of use, then comparison groups, then randomized trials. Each will be registered before it starts and published whatever it finds. The research behind each part of AMP is in our report, and AMP is open source.

them: Your child loves puzzles and wants hard problems, taught through comic-style books in a set order.
amp: You want assessment, teaching and review in the same practice, with no separate tests.
You want a hint at every problem that gives the first step, not the solution.
You want learned skills to keep coming back in practice.
Your learner is at different levels in different parts of math, or past Level 5.

questions.question: How is AMP different from Beast Academy?
questions.answer: Beast Academy places a learner with a test, then by default teaches lesson by lesson in a fixed order, with a test at the end of each chapter [4][5]. AMP has no separate test: every answer sets the next problem, each problem carries its own teaching, and learned skills return in ordinary practice.

questions.question: Does Beast Academy work?
questions.answer: Two studies by outside evaluators, done for its maker, report positive associations. In one district, users scored higher on the MAP math test than matched non-users, many of them in gifted and high-ability programs [10]. In another, more minutes of use went with higher scores, with no group of non-users [11]. We found no randomized trial [13][14].

questions.question: Can a learner use both?
questions.answer: Yes. They are separate programs. AMP places a learner from their first answers, whatever else they use.
